Article Title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
Article Text:
After bringing all crew members into the ‘citadel’, the master of the Golden Arsenal sought help from the Indian Navy, which responded swiftly to the distress call (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled after the captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vessel’s “citadel” and sought assistance from the Indian Navy A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment, where crew members can take refuge during a pirate attack. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel.Sharing this incident at the National Port Security Conference this week, Captain Vikram Singh Manhas, deputy nautical adviser at DGMA (maritime regulator), urged all crew members and masters to remain vigilant and follow preventive measures prescribed under best management practices (BMP), amid a rise in piracy incidents.Four vessels are held hostage by Somali pirates at present, three of which have Indian crew members aboard.One of the vessels has one Indian seafarer, while the other two have five and 11 Indian crew, respectively.Highlighting the significance of prevention in such cases, Manhas said that once a vessel is held by pirates, everything is dependent upon the negotiations with the pirates and that the government is working to ensure the safe release of Indian seafarers.In the direction of ensuring their safety, the government is set to launch a dashboard on August 15 to track every Indian seafarer on any ship. Additionally, shipping and ports minister Sarbananda Sonowal Saturday launched e-Samudra, a digital platform integrating services for seafarers, shipping companies, ports and other maritime stakeholders, and said, “Every Indian seafarer must be safe, respected and supported as India strengthens its position as a global maritime power. ”
Article Summary: After bringing all crew members into the ‘citadel’, the master of the golden arsenal sought help from the indian navy. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel. Four vessels are held hostage by somali pirates at present, three of which have indian crew members aboard.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Rahul Gandhi Saturday sparred over the women's reservation bill, when Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to support the women's quota, and the latter shot back that it was passed by Parliament in 2023.The to and fro started when Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju seized upon a video of Rahul Gandhi on X in which he, espousing the cause of women's empowerment, said no country can progress without its women having the freedom to express themselves.To corner the LoP, Rijiju replied, "This seems to be a positive message from Congress. Article Title: “I'm going to kick his a**”: Austin Reaves throws a huge challenge to Lakers brother Luka Doncic in a candid joke
Article Text:
Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Image via: Joe Murphy/ NBAE via Getty Images

Luka Doncic's leadership and the Lakers' new-look roster

How Reaves and Doncic's numbers stack up entering 2026-27

Austin Reaves is already trash-talking Luka Doncic ahead of the Los Angeles Lakers' minicamp in Slovenia, and golf is the battlefield. Speaking at his 2026 Rigorer Basketball Camp, Reaves made clear he's arriving with a plan. "I'm going to kick his a** in golf," he said, before pivoting to the real point of the trip: getting a retooled Lakers roster comfortable with each other before training camp opens.The four-day camp, running Aug. 20 to Aug. 24, marks the first real gathering for a Lakers team that looks almost nothing like the one LeBron James left behind.Austin Reaves was in Hong Kong on his annual China tour when he was asked about the trip, and his answer doubled as both a joke and a mission statement. Golf has become his preferred way of getting under Luka Doncic's skin, and by his own account, it's one of the only competitions he's ever had a real shot at winning against his co-star.Doncic only picked up golf back in March, pushed into it by Reaves and James. He's a six-time All-Star coming off a scoring title and a fourth-place MVP finish, but a beginner with a driver in his hand. Reaves has reportedly beaten him at everything they've tried except basketball, which happens to be the one that decides games.The minicamp itself is Doncic's idea, and it says something about where he sees himself now that James is gone. He's hosting teammates in Ljubljana, mixing basketball workouts with sightseeing and golf, and using the week to fast-track chemistry a roster this reshaped badly needs. Doncic posted about the trip himself, writing that he's "looking forward to the time together" and excited to show his new teammates where he's from.The roster he's welcoming barely resembles last season's group. Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Kevon Looney, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Jaden Hardy are all new additions, brought in as general manager Rob Pelinka reshaped the team around Doncic's strengths. Rookie Cameron Carr is the only player who won't make it, held back by mandatory NBA rookie orientation.The two are now unquestionably the Lakers' core. Doncic averaged 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists last season, numbers that carried Los Angeles even as the roster around him churned. Reaves backed that up with 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists, production that earned him a four-year, $180 million contract this summer.That extension, paired with James' departure, settled any question about who the Lakers are building around. Head coach JJ Redick inherits a team with a clear top two and eight new faces still learning where they fit. A week in Slovenia, golf trash talk included, is Doncic's answer to how fast that gets figured out.
Article Summary: The los angeles lakers are hosting a minicamp in slovenia. Austin reaves says he's going to "kick his a** in golf" luka doncic is the only player who can beat reaves on the golf course. The four-day camp runs from aug. 20 to aug. 24.

Article Title: Sarfaraz Khan's cryptic post goes viral amid continued India snub: 'I may not fit in, but I'll fight'

Sarfaraz Khan

From Test century to selection uncertainty

NEW DELHI: Sarfaraz Khan 's place in India's Test plans appears increasingly uncertain, but the Mumbai batter has made it clear that he is not ready to give up.Amid his continued absence from the national squad, Sarfaraz shared a cryptic Instagram story recently, posting a still from the 2019 Telugu film Jersey with a message that appeared to reflect his current situation."I may not fit in, but I'll fight with everything I've got."The post quickly caught the attention of Indian cricket fans, coming just days before India begin their two-Test series against Sri Lanka. Sarfaraz was once again overlooked for the series despite boasting one of the strongest first-class records among India's middle-order contenders.The 28-year-old has averaged an extraordinary 64.73 in 62 first-class matches but has played only six Tests for India. He was part of India's squad for the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy but did not feature in a single game Down Under.Sarfaraz's omission is particularly notable given the impact he made during India's home series against New Zealand in 2024.He scored a memorable 150 in the first Test in Bengaluru, one of the few positives from a series in which India suffered a historic 0-3 whitewash at home. However, he struggled to replicate that success in the remainder of the series and managed a highest score of only 11 thereafter.He was subsequently included in India's squad for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy but did not feature in the series. Since then, opportunities to reclaim his place have remained scarce.Sarfaraz was also part of the India A setup during the England tour but remained on the fringes, suggesting that the selectors currently have other options ahead of him in the Test pecking order.Fitness had also been a recurring talking point around Sarfaraz, but the Mumbai batter has since undergone a significant transformation, shedding weight and improving his conditioning.He also returned to the IPL in 2026 after going unsold in the previous two auctions. Chennai Super Kings handed him an opportunity and Sarfaraz responded with 161 runs at a strike rate of 169.47, including two half-centuries.India are currently playing a three-day warm-up game in Colombo ahead of the series, with the first Test scheduled to begin in Galle on August 15 and the second at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo.

WWE Hall of Famer Hulk Hogan passed away at the age of 71, leaving behind a great wrestling legacy and a void in the hearts of WWE fans. The veteran WWE star, known for his wrestling prowess and charisma, passed away on July 24, 2025, at his residence in Clearwater, Florida. While the wrestling icon is no longer with us, his larger-than-life persona recently made an unusual return to the ring through a wrestler determined to carry “The Immortal One’s” spirit. WWE Hall of Famer Hulk Hogan seems to have returned to in-ring action in a way after a wrestler, Temu Hogan, who appears to be a big fan of the pro wrestling legend, has taken it upon himself to plan the return of the legendary icon, according to ITR Wrestler.In a video circulated online, it has been identified that, sporting a white wig, a long white moustache, and white trunks, the wrestler entered the ring channeling the legendary WWE Hall of Famer.The wrestler has been identified as Temu Hogan, a clear parody and tribute to the former WWE Champion.As per reports, the wrestler in the frame is called Temu Hogan. He was in action at Insane Wrestling Revolution for the Kangaroo Cup. The show took place at Grizzly’s Bar and Grill in Wyandotte, Michigan, where Temu Hogan, who was carrying The Immortal One within him, actually went on to win the Kangaroo Cup with Sam Beale.Hulk Hogan, born Terry Gene Bollea, is one of the most iconic figures in professional wrestling history. Known for his larger-than-life persona, charismatic presence, and legendary catchphrases, Hogan became a household name during the 1980s and 1990s in the wrestling community.Throughout his career, Hogan won multiple world championships, headlined numerous WrestleMania events, and later helped transform WCW. He was a favourite among his fans due to his signature moves and red-and-yellow attire. Due to his huge contributions to WWE, Hogan was inducted as a WWE Hall of Famer in the year 2005 and inducted a second time in 2020.Earlier, following Hulk Hogan’s death, speculation was raised by her daughter, Brooke Hogan, that a possible foul play might have been involved in the WWE icon’s sudden death, which led the Clearwater Police to take the investigation seriously.However, they have clearly ruled out that there was no criminal wrongdoing involved after the Clearwater Police Department officially ruled out Hogan’s death as natural, and they have closed the probe.WWE Hall of Famer Hulk Hogan’s funeral took place on August 5, 2025, at his Clearwater residence in Florida, and he was laid to rest in a private funeral in Clearwater, Florida, 12 days after his death.

Article Title: "Blow up Messi with four bombs": Shocking police files uncover alleged suicide bombing plot targeting Lionel Messi

A chilling security dossier has revealed that Lionel Messi was at the center of an alleged terror plot during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, exposing the hidden dangers that unfolded behind one of football's biggest celebrations. While millions watched the tournament for unforgettable moments on the pitch, investigators were reportedly racing against time to stop multiple threats that could have turned the global event into a tragedy. Newly surfaced details paint a disturbing picture of the extraordinary security operation that protected players, officials, and supporters throughout the competition.The 2026 FIFA World Cup, jointly hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, delivered memorable football before Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the final to lift the trophy. Away from the stadium lights, however, security agencies were reportedly dealing with a series of credible threats aimed at the tournament.According to reports, a joint security network led by the FBI and the Centre for International Police Cooperation (IPCC) worked throughout the competition to identify and neutralize potential attacks before they could be carried out.Among the most alarming discoveries was an alleged plot targeting Lionel Messi. A police dossier reportedly revealed that one individual openly declared his intention to carry out a suicide bombing inside Atlanta's stadium. According to The Sun, the suspect allegedly posted the following message on X:"I'm going to walk into the Atlanta stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs stuck in my body."Authorities reportedly treated the threat with the highest level of seriousness. Messi was said to be the most frequently targeted player during the tournament, reflecting both his global profile and the enormous public attention surrounding Argentina's legendary captain.Investigators also examined another serious incident involving a phone call made to Dallas airport. According to reports, the caller claimed that he and two other people were heading toward a stadium carrying homemade bombs and an AR-15. The message allegedly stated that both police officers and players were intended targets, while specifically mentioning Messi by name.The reported threats highlighted the enormous responsibility placed on security personnel during an event that attracted millions of spectators and worldwide television audiences.The dossier reportedly shows that Messi was not the only football icon under threat during the tournament.Cristiano Ronaldo was also subjected to repeated security concerns throughout the World Cup. Reports claim that on June 14, a FIFA employee alerted authorities after noticing a suspicious individual attempting to obtain details about the Portuguese superstar's accommodation. Similar incidents were reportedly recorded in Toronto, Houston, and Miami, leading officials to maintain heightened protection around the veteran forward.The security concerns extended beyond the players. French referee François Letexier was reportedly bombarded with around 6,000 threatening messages on WhatsApp during the tournament, underscoring the intense pressure faced by match officials as well.Despite those alarming challenges, the competition concluded without any reported terror attack disrupting the event. The successful efforts of international law enforcement agencies ensured that the focus ultimately remained on football rather than fear.Meanwhile, questions continue to surround Messi's international future after Argentina's runner-up finish. Argentine Football Association president Claudio "Chiqui" Tapia recently stressed that the decision rests entirely with the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, saying:«"It's a purely personal decision. We have to leave him in peace and give him space. It was a great World Cup, we enjoyed it a lot and we're proud. I'll remember every hug after every match because, for me, it;s personal. It reflects the affection and the relationship we have."»With 207 international appearances, 125 goals, a World Cup title in 2022, and two Copa América triumphs, Messi has already secured his place among football's greatest players. Whether the 2026 final proves to be his last appearance for Argentina remains a decision only he can make.

One individual allegedly declared his intention to carry out a suicide bombing inside atlanta's stadium. Cristiano ronaldo was also subjected to repeated security concerns throughout the tournament.

Jade Cargill’s career continues to evolve in WWE

Jade Cargill’s climb to the top of WWE is very different from the traditional route many professional wrestlers take. And not years on the independent wrestling circuit competing, she developed first as an elite athlete through basketball. Her time on the court provided her the physical base, discipline and competitive drive that would later be a staple of her wrestling persona.Cargill also had an educational and professional career outside of sports entertainment before becoming one of the most recognisable stars in WWE. She obtained a master’s degree in child psychology and worked with children, but ultimately decided that professional wrestling was a better opportunity to combine her athletic abilities, personality and ambitions. Her transition from basketball and psychology to wrestling has become one of the most unusual career changes in modern WWE.Jade Cargill’s journey as an athlete predates her professional wrestling career on her career path. She became a basketball fan early on, even playing at the college level, suiting up for the Jacksonville Dolphins of Jacksonville University.During her time at Jacksonville University, Cargill was a forward and guard. Through her college experience, she also got a taste of the demands of competitive sports, regimented training, physical competition and performance pressure.Basketball also taught me a few qualities that would later become valuable in the wrestling ring. Explosiveness, balance, strength and coordination are key in both sports, and Cargill’s imposing physical presence quickly became one of her defining characteristics after taking up wrestling.After her collegiate career, she was able to play basketball professionally overseas. Cargill has experience competing in France and competing outside the United States.This period was significant in that it confirmed that her athletic career did not begin with the sport of wrestling. But before she got into the entertainment world of WWE, she had already experienced the discipline it takes to pursue sport professionally.While basketball provided Cargill with a good athletic background, it didn’t end up being her career path. The economics and opportunities of professional women’s basketball influenced my decision to look at other avenues.Instead of diving straight into wrestling, Cargill veered yet again into education and child psychology. That decision makes her future WWE career all the more unique because her professional background extended far beyond sports.Cargill’s decision to go into child psychology was one of the biggest departures from her ultimate WWE persona. She didn't jump into the professional wrestling business right away, but instead went back to school and built a career helping kids.Cargill has a master’s degree in child psychology, an impressive academic credential to add to her resume. Her education showed she was not one to keep her ambitions confined to athletics and had forged a professional identity beyond the sporting realm.Cargill eventually got into pro wrestling thanks to her relationship with WWE Hall of Famer Mark Henry. Henry saw her physical potential and helped open the door to wrestling training.So her move was more than a change of sport. It was about learning a whole new brand of athletic entertainment while building a larger-than-life personality.Cargill’s foray into pro wrestling began with All Elite Wrestling, and her swift ascent paved the way for her eventual WWE career. Cargill signed with AEW in 2020 and quickly became one of the promotion’s most visually distinctive performers. Her presentation was strong, confident and with an imposing superhero-like appearance different from many other wrestlers on the roster.Cargill jumped from AEW to WWE in September 2023 and immediately became one of the most watched signings in women’s pro wrestling.WWE didn't just put her straight into regular weekly competition; instead, the company spent time creating anticipation around her arrival, highlighting her look, her athletic background, and her past accomplishments.Cargill debuted in WWE in-ring at the 2024 Royal Rumble, and the star turn gave her an even bigger global audience and marked the next step in her evolution from promising wrestler to established WWE attraction.Her career demonstrated the significance of her basketball journey. Strength, speed, discipline, competitiveness, the same qualities that made her a great athlete could be repackaged for pro wrestling.Cargill’s appeal is more than her wrestling accomplishments, because her career represents the increasingly diverse paths athletes can take into sports entertainment.Usually, wrestlers will work their way up through years of independent wrestling before graduating to bigger promotions. Cargill chose a different path. Her athletic background was in basketball; her educational and professional background was in psychology.AEW gave her national exposure, and WWE gave her the platform to be a global star.The switch also demonstrates how much physical presentation matters in today’s pro wrestling. Cargill had the physique and athleticism to distinguish herself from the rest of the field, allowing WWE to showcase her as a star attraction as she continued to hone her in-ring skills.In the grand scheme of things, Cargill’s WWE journey is a relatively recent chapter for many established wrestling stars. Moving from AEW to WWE was a huge career decision, but it also spoke to the size of her ambitions.The biggest change has been the size of the deck. WWE opens doors for Cargill, allowing her to reach a global audience and some of the biggest events in the business, outside the traditional world of wrestling competition.
Article Summary: Jade cargill’s path from aew to wwe transformed her career. She developed first as an elite athlete through basketball. Her time on the court provided her the physical base, discipline and competitive drive that would later be a staple of her wrestling persona. She also had an educational and professional career outside of sports entertainment.

Article Title: Wolves fans mourn the death of Phil Parkes as legendary goalkeeper passes away at 79 after 18-year Molineux career

Fans pay tribute to the Wolves Hall of Famer Phil Parkes

Wolverhampton Wanderers have paid tribute to legendary goalkeeper Phil Parkes, who has died at the age of 79. Parkes spent 18 years with the club and made 382 appearances for the first team. He was later inducted into the Wolves Hall of Fame.Known affectionately as ‘Lofty’ because of his 6ft 4in height, Parkes remained closely connected with Wolves after retiring. The club described him as a larger-than-life figure and a true hero. Wolves also expressed their sympathy to his family and loved ones and said further tributes would be announced.Phil Parkes began his Wolves journey as a schoolboy in 1960. He was only 13 at the time. He turned professional in 1964 after progressing through the club’s youth and reserve teams.His first-team debut came in November 1966 against Preston North End. He made an immediate impact by saving a penalty in a 3-2 victory.Parkes soon became an important part of Bill McGarry’s Wolves side. He was known for his consistency and reliability. During the early 1970s, he played 127 consecutive league matches.The run remains a Wolves club record.The goalkeeper also played a major role in one of the most memorable European campaigns in the club’s history. Wolves reached their first European final in the 1971-72 UEFA Cup. Parkes saved two penalties against Ferencvaros in the semi-final.Wolves eventually faced Tottenham Hotspur in the final. The Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy has taken another turn, this time putting the spotlight on the NFL media itself. Podcast host Nikki Gist has questioned why more female reporters have not publicly addressed the allegations and the wider questions surrounding Russini’s work. Her comments come as The Athletic’s internal investigation into Russini remains unfinished months after it began. The lack of a public conclusion has already frustrated fans, while Gist’s criticism has raised a broader issue: when a major media controversy involves one of their own, how much accountability should fellow journalists demand?Gist’s criticism is aimed less at revisiting every detail of the Russini-Vrabel story and more at what she sees as a lack of scrutiny from other journalists. She specifically questioned why female reporters have not been more vocal about the situation.“To all the female reporters staying [expletive] quiet,” Gist said. “Why is that? Why are you all quiet?”Her argument is straightforward. Journalists are expected to question people and institutions when there are legitimate concerns about conduct, reporting standards or accountability. Gist believes that responsibility should not disappear simply because the person under scrutiny is a fellow journalist.She also challenged the idea that Russini’s reputation as a respected reporter should shield her from questions. That is where the debate becomes more complicated. Criticism of Russini does not establish that every allegation against her is true, and silence from other reporters does not necessarily prove they are protecting her.Still, Gist’s comments have landed at a sensitive time for the NFL media industry. The controversy has already moved beyond Russini and Vrabel, with growing attention on how sports outlets investigate their own employees.The Athletic opened an internal investigation into Russini’s reporting on April 11, shortly after the controversy became public. Russini resigned from the publication on April 14. Months later, the findings have still not been released publicly.That delay has become a story of its own.The Athletic executive editor Steven Ginsberg previously said the investigation would take “a few more weeks.” Those weeks have now stretched much longer, leaving fans to speculate about what is taking so long. Some have suggested the outlet is hoping public interest fades, although there is no confirmed evidence that this is the reason for the delay.That distinction matters. An internal review can involve interviews, records and legal considerations that are not visible to the public. A lengthy process does not, by itself, prove wrongdoing or a cover-up.But transparency still matters. Until The Athletic explains where the investigation stands, the unanswered questions will continue to feed speculation. For Gist and others pressing for clarity, the issue is no longer simply what happened between Russini and Vrabel. It is also whether the sports media industry is willing to apply the same level of scrutiny inward that it routinely applies to athletes, coaches and teams.

England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has thrown his weight behind the England and Wales Cricket Board's decision to hand Joe Root the Test captaincy once again, insisting Harry Brook 's opportunity to lead the side in the longest format will arrive in due course.The ECB's decision to bring Root back as Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement came as a surprise, with many expecting vice-captain Brook to take over. His first spell as Test captain ended amid mounting criticism before Ben Stokes replaced him, but following Stokes' retirement, the ECB has turned back to its most prolific Test batter to guide the side through a new era.The leadership reshuffle has also extended to the coaching setup. The lasting legacy of the Tkachuk family in American hockey

Few families in the United States have had as much of an impact on the modern game of hockey as the Tkachuk family. The family name has become synonymous with elite talent, fierce competitiveness and leadership over three generations of impact, starting with Keith Tkachuk and continuing with his sons Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk. Their story isn’t just statistics or championships, but building a culture that blends ability with physicality, accountability and love for the game.Keith Tkachuk blazed a trail with an amazing 18-season NHL career that made him one of the greatest American-born power forwards in league history. The legacy has been lifted even higher by Matthew Tkachuk of the Florida Panthers and Brady Tkachuk, who followed his brother to Florida after making his mark as captain of the Ottawa Senators. The trio has helped redefine what American hockey players can do at the NHL and international levels.Keith Tkachuk was already one of the NHL's premier power forwards long before Matthew and Brady were household names. Big Walt, as he was known, added elite offensive production, toughness, consistency and leadership to an 18-season NHL career.Keith spent his entire career with the Winnipeg Jets, Phoenix Coyotes, St.Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. In the 1996-97 season, he became the first American-born player to lead the NHL in goals, a sign of the growing influence of American players in a league long dominated by Canadian talent.Keith may not have done the most for hockey by scoring 538 goals, but rather by the environment he provided for Matthew and Brady growing up.Like many former professional athletes, Keith never put huge expectations on his children and always stressed the enjoyment of the game. Hockey was still something to get excited about, not something to press for, and it gave both sons a chance to develop naturally, while preserving their love for competition.Hell was to pay in the Tkachuk household. Whether playing hockey in the driveway, competing in backyard games or watching NHL contests together, each activity was a learning opportunity. Keith encouraged both boys to compete against each other but also respect their teammates and the opposition.Communication was also a defining strength of the family. Keith taught hockey IQ, preparation and accountability through everyday conversations, not long lectures. That showed later in Matthew’s emotional leadership and Brady’s ability to inspire teammates.Keith also made certain that his sons knew that talent alone would never guarantee success. Hard work, consistency and resilience were non-negotiable values throughout their development.Matt Tkachuk stepped onto the professional hockey scene loaded with expectations, as the son of one of the greatest NHL players in American history. Rather than getting bogged down in those comparisons, he quickly established himself as one of the league’s top power forwards.The Calgary Flames picked Matthew sixth overall in the 2016 NHL Draft, and he quickly showed the scoring touch, creativity and physical edge that had become synonymous with the Tkachuk name. Everything changed when he was traded to the Florida Panthers in 2022. Matthew quickly became the heart and soul of the Panthers, helping turn the franchise into a perennial Stanley Cup contender.While Matthew may have gotten to the NHL first, Brady Tkachuk quickly demonstrated that he possessed many of the same qualities that paved the way for his father and older brother’s success. Drafted fourth overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2018 NHL Draft, Brady quickly established himself as one of the league’s most fearless young forwards.Those leadership qualities paid off in November 2021 when Brady was named the 10th captain in Ottawa Senators franchise history. Only 22 years old, he was handed the reins to guide one of the NHL’s youngest rosters through a tough time. His teammates often praised his consistency, accountability and desire to lead by example, not just talk.Brady’s offence just kept getting better, too. Multiple 30-goal seasons and career-best point totals made him more than just a physical forward. Brady, like his father and brother, proved that toughness and elite offensive talent could be found in the same player.His next trade to the Florida Panthers brought the Tkachuk brothers back together at the NHL level for one of hockey’s most compelling storylines. The two became teammates, fulfilling a childhood dream, and giving the Panthers two of the league’s most competitive power forwards on the same roster.There have been plenty of famous family names in pro hockey, but few have built a legacy quite like the Tkachuks.
